## Context / Problem
Fixture setup is 47% of the `tests/interfaces` tier wall-clock: a serial run measured 361.4s setup vs 391.0s call vs 13.9s teardown across 1385 tests — 261 ms of setup per test.

The cause is `rebar_repo` (tests/interfaces/conftest.py:36), a function-scoped fixture that per test runs mkdir, `git init`, two `git config`, `rebar.init_repo()`, and `git commit --allow-empty`. 589 test functions request it. Measured cost 306 ms, of which `rebar.init_repo()` alone is 268 ms (88%) and spawns 54 git subprocesses; with the fixture's own 4 that is 58 process spawns per test. The suite is spawn-bound, not IO-bound (tier-wide `sys` 335s exceeds `user` 218s).

This matters because the macOS pytest cell is the Gerrit Verified gate critical path (~18.6m) AND holds one of only 5 org-wide concurrent macOS runner slots, so shortening it helps twice.

## Approach
Build the initialized repo ONCE per xdist worker in a session-scoped fixture, then give each test a `shutil.copytree` copy. Measured 306 ms -> 22.3 ms including the pointer fix-up (13.7x).

A copied store is NOT usable as-is: `rebar.init_repo` creates the ticket store as a git LINKED WORKTREE, and two files embed the template's absolute path — `.tickets-tracker/.git` and `.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker/gitdir`. An exhaustive scan (no size limit, binaries included) found no others; `commondir` is relative and `.git/config` carries no paths.

CRITICAL, and the reason this ticket exists rather than a one-line change: a BARE `git worktree repair` run from the copy is a silent NO-OP. It validates by path existence, and because the template still exists on disk both pointers look valid. The copy then keeps using the TEMPLATE's object store and `refs/heads/tickets`; a single write in the copy advances the template's ref. Under `-n 3 --dist worksteal` that is N workers sharing one ref and one object database — an unreproducible flake spray that ordinary assertions cannot see, because `rebar list` reads worktree FILES, not refs. This ticket therefore rewrites the two pointer files explicitly and adds a positive guard assertion so the failure mode can never regress silently.

Rejected alternative: bare `git worktree repair` — proven to be a no-op here.
Rejected alternative: session-scoped SHARED repo (no copy) — destroys per-test isolation outright.
Rejected alternative: migrating the ~20 module-local store-building fixtures in this same change — deferred to a follow-up so the guard mechanism lands and is measured on one fixture first.

## Scope
- `tests/interfaces/conftest.py` — add a session-scoped template fixture and a `_clone_template` helper (ONE place the pointer fix can be wrong); rewrite `rebar_repo` to copy + fix + assert.
- `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` — NEW: the sentinel test for the shared-gitdir failure mode.

Only `rebar_repo` migrates. The ~20 module-local fixtures that duplicate the same dance are a deliberate follow-up (they are the larger share of the remaining win).

### Residual coverage of the build-from-scratch path
Collapsing 589 incidental `init_repo` invocations to one per xdist worker removes INCIDENTAL coverage of the scratch-init path, so the deliberate coverage must be named accurately:
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_init_idempotent_scratch.py` and `tests/interfaces/store/test_e4_init.py` DO call `init_repo` at runtime — these are the real from-scratch runtime coverage and must keep building from scratch, not from the template.
- `tests/unit/test_init_no_hardcoded_tracker.py` does NOT exercise the runtime path. It contains only `test_no_hardcoded_tracker_dir_literal_in_init_code()`, which reads the source and walks the AST for hardcoded path literals — zero `init_repo` calls, zero subprocesses. It is a static guard and must not be counted as runtime coverage. (An earlier draft of this plan claimed it exercised the build-from-scratch path; that was factually wrong.)

## Testing
The migrated fixture must be PROVEN to isolate, and the proof must itself be proven to be a genuine sentinel rather than a test that passes regardless.

New test `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` asserts that a `rebar_repo` store resolves its git common dir INSIDE its own copy (`git -C <repo>/.tickets-tracker rev-parse --git-common-dir`), and that a write in one store does not advance any other store's `refs/heads/tickets`.

RED/GREEN bracket (required, not optional): temporarily replace the two-file pointer rewrite with a bare `subprocess.run(["git","-C",copy,"worktree","repair"])`, run the sentinel, and CONFIRM IT FAILS. Then restore the fix-up and confirm it passes. Without observing the RED, the sentinel is unproven and the AC is satisfied only in letter.

The existing 589 consumers are the regression suite: they must pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar_repo` yields a store whose `.tickets-tracker` git common dir resolves inside that test's own directory, asserted in the fixture itself so every consumer is guarded.
- [ ] The sentinel test is DEMONSTRATED RED: with the pointer fix-up replaced by a bare `git worktree repair`, `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -q` FAILS; with the fix-up restored it passes. Both observations recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] Writing a ticket in one `rebar_repo` does not advance any other store's `refs/heads/tickets`, including the template's.
- [ ] The template path is realpath-resolved before substitution (macOS reports `/private/tmp/...`).
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/interfaces -q` passes with the same collected/passed counts as before the change.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/store/test_init_idempotent_scratch.py` and `tests/interfaces/store/test_e4_init.py` still build from scratch (not from the template) and pass.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
